text.p: Australian-interest commodity prices slumped at the end of the week with gold hitting fresh three-year lows on talk of central bank sales, copper falling on profit taking, wheat easing on ample supplies and oil closing weaker on milder weather in major consumption areas.
The CRB index closed 1.32 points lower at 236.75.

LME copper ended Friday's afternoon kerb at the bottom of its range, hit by a bout of end-of-week profit-taking after prices failed to attack the upside. The other metals also gave up modest gains, winding down ahead of the weekend.
Three months copper finished the afternoon kerb at $2,239, down $18 from Thursday's close.
"The market was concerned when copper failed to break above $2,270," said analyst Martin Squires of broker Rudolf Wolff.
The close, though, was still a gain on the week after fears of persistent tightness sent shorts scurrying several days ago.
Nearby spreads have consistently traded at LME imposed limits for over a week, but spreads were expected to deflate after the prompt date on February 19.
But tightness is now extending beyond the February date, shown by the Feb/threes spread which flared this week from a low of $35/40 to $102/112 by the end of business on Friday.
This is keeping the cash/threes wide, ending at $203/$218.
Players may have a go at lower levels on Monday, but the hefty backwardations should offer support, analysts said.
"I wouldn't become concerned unless prices fell below $2,200," Squires said.
Nickel eased back after hitting a fresh 7-1/2 month high of $7,960 in the morning on the back of a hefty stocks decline.
It ended the kerb $80 weaker at $7,800, but the softer finish still represents a gain on the week.
"It has had a big rally and needed to correct back," Squires said. Zinc ended the day $3 easier at $1,183 after hitting a fresh two-year high of $1,196 in the morning.
The next significant targets are the psychological $1,200 mark and the January 1995 peak of $1,239.
Aluminium slipped to the bottom of a $1,600-$1,650 range it has held for the past few weeks.
Three months closed the day down $19.50 at $1,603. Lead finished $4 off at $675 and tin ended $15 easier at $5,875.

New York precious metals futures ended higher Friday, except for gold which fell to new three year lows on more talk of central bank sales, rumored hedge fund activity, and some nervous producer hedging, traders said. COMEX April gold ended down $1.10 an ounce at $343.40, after posting a new contract low at $339.40 intraday. In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $341.50/00, compared to the London Friday afternoon fix at $339.75, the lowest fix since April 22, 1993. Spot gold closed in New York Thursday quoted $342.80/30.

CBOT wheat futures closed mostly lower, led by March, with a new contract low of $3.54-1/2 per bushel set in that month on persistent reminders of adequate supplies worldwide. The previous low for March was $3.56 and was set Wednesday.

NYMEX crude continued its sharp decline Friday as the need for refined product diminished amid declining heating oil use and the peak summer demand season for gasoline still too far away. March crude settled off 87 cents a barrel at $22.23, declining for the fourth consecutive session and losing $1.92 a barrel for the week.
